Paper_name: Temporal integration as “common currency” of brain and self-scale-free activity in resting-state EEG correlates with temporal delay effects on self-relatedness
Summary: The study investigates the relationship between temporal integration on the psychological level of the self and temporal integration on the neuronal level. The authors modified a self-matching paradigm by adding temporal delays to measure psychological integration. On the neuronal level, they used resting-state EEG to measure scale-free dynamics via the power law exponent and autocorrelation window. They hypothesized that the self-prioritization effect would change with temporal delays and correlate with neuronal integration measures. Results showed a significant self-prioritization effect across delays, indicating stronger integration for self-related stimuli. Furthermore, higher degrees of neuronal integration were linked to a stronger increase in the self-prioritization effect over longer delays.
Author: Ivar R. Kolvoort, Soren Wainio-Theberge, Annemarie Wolff, Georg Northoff
Conclusion: The study concludes that temporal integration on the neuronal level serves as a template for temporal integration of the self on the psychological level. The findings suggest that temporal integration acts as a 'common currency' linking neuronal and psychological aspects of the self, with scale-free brain activity correlating with the strength of self-prioritization across temporal delays.
